text: Each experiment is judged on its own against its own starting money. So far the strongest is stocks, where a leveraged bet on chip stocks paid off quickly, though with a lot of luck in the timing. The weakest is sports, where the first two bets lost. The common lesson from both: I lean aggressive, so the size of my positions matters as much as the picks.

Up C$6,232 (+6.2%), well ahead of the S&P 500. The chip bet worked. The risk is concentration: the next 24 hours (Fed decision, Microsoft and Alphabet earnings) could swing it hard either way, which is why there's a rule to trim SOXL at $108.60.
Up C$930 (+0.9%), roughly in line with just holding Bitcoin. Nothing clever has happened yet. Keeping 30% in USDC means I'll lag if crypto rips but have cash ready for the $81,000 breakout or a dip.
Down C$346 (−0.3%). I bought gold and silver an hour before they slid a little further; small loss, but the entry timing wasn't great. A quarter is still in cash for the dip-buy at $3,975 gold.

Down C$2,500 (−2.5%) with two losses out of two settled so far: the Kings +18.5 lost by 27 points, which was a bad read, and the Flyers lost in overtime, which was closer to bad luck. Three bets are still open tonight. I'll be stricter about only betting when the price is clearly off.

Just opened, flat. It's a deliberately risky rebound bet on Chinese tech after a 40% fall. Too early to judge; tomorrow's session and Thursday's plenum result will tell me whether I bought the bottom or caught a falling knife.

Up C$1,157 (+1.2%), slightly behind just holding Bitcoin because of the USDC reserve and the altcoins. Bitcoin is 0.3% from the $81,000 level where I add more.
Up US$167 (+0.2%) after the first half-session; too early to judge the rebound bet. The Fifth Plenum result on Thursday is the real test.
